gate_1_overlap.claim: where both routes are valid, the hand-over route's reading (the solve holding the plug at nine times its permeability, its line moved to three times its sqrt(K)/h) agrees with the resolved route's lumen_flux
gate_1_overlap.kind: equality within a line: each route is checked against the series closed form by its own gate; this one checks the reading against the two-way solve
gate_1_overlap.case: porous_handover_cases.overlap(dh, root, interior): CI at D/h 16, half a diameter in a period of two, sqrt(K)/h 0.03 at 0.1h and 0.01h; the probe at one diameter in a period of four, D/h 16 and 32, sqrt(K)/h 0.003 (0.1h only), 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, both interiors

prediction.value: ratio - 1 = -f + e, f = 1024 (sqrt(K)/h)^2 / (D/h)^2 the held plug's feedback (the flux nine K passes over the open tube's, less K's), e the reading's face error against the solve's
prediction.basis: derived (f, from the series of the held plug's resistance and the open tube's) and measured-before (e: +0.3 / +0.7 % in exploration; #264's face drop within 3.5 %)
prediction.why: the reading takes the solved drop, which the held plug sets as R_held / (R_held + R_open) of the drive; below 8 K_held / R^2 = 0.01 the drop is the plug's within f

gate_1_overlap.metric: the reading over the resolved lumen_flux, both from the real node's steady step

control.plant: the reading's permeability doubled (READING_K2; ratio near 2, f under 0.04); the face pressures' signs flipped (FACE_SIGN; the drop's sign and size change)
control.resolution: a reading off by f + the line, some 2 to 6 %: the K x2 plant is about 25 times it

gate_1_overlap.if_wrong: a ratio outside the line at f under 0.01 would mean the face pressures do not carry the plug's drop (the planes' placement, the drive's term over L + W): the face reading is re-measured against the series before anything is tuned
gate_1_overlap.cannot_discriminate_if: both arms' solves flagged (stagnated or capped): the row is then reported unmeasured

gate_2_forced.claim: flow forced through a plug below the line (a fixed inflow, a plug closing the single tube) raises forced_flagged on every draw; a pressure-driven tube, a plug leaving a gap, and two parallel tubes from one inlet with one closed by the plug and a fixed inflow upstream do not
gate_2_forced.kind: acceptance (a flag), structural: the topology says where a law fixes the flux through the plug, the comparison says the reading fell short of it
gate_2_forced.case: porous_handover_cases.vessel (forced: inflow, plug closing; gap: radius 0.25; pressure: a resistance at both ends), occluded_twin, tube_reading (periodic, a body force)

prediction.value: forced 50/50 flagged; the periodic tube, the gap and the twin rig 0/50 each
prediction.basis: derived: in the forced case the reading is K / K_line of the forced flux, under (1 - FORCED_LINE) = 0.9 of it for every draw (K under 0.5 K_line); in the quiet cases the topology answers no
prediction.why: a held plug obeys its own Darcy relation whatever drives it, so only the vessel's topology tells a fixed flux from a driven one

gate_2_forced.metric: forced_flagged at the run's last step

control.plant: the comparison disabled (FORCED_OFF: the forced case missed on every draw); the topology answering forced for every region (FORCED_EVERYWHERE: every quiet case flagged, the reading K / K_line of the held plug's flux)
control.resolution: a yes/no flag; the comparison's own margin is FORCED_LINE (0.1) against a deficit of 1 - K / K_line, at least 0.5 on the draws

gate_2_forced.if_wrong: a quiet case flagged means the topology test or the gap test is wrong for it; a forced draw missed means the drop was read as unresolved (DROP_RESOLVED) or the section flux missed the plug
gate_2_forced.cannot_discriminate_if: every quiet case is quiet only because the topology answered no: the FORCED_EVERYWHERE control is what shows the comparison would have flagged them

gate_3_carried_depth.claim: for a plug far below the interior's permeability, the reading's error against the series closed form is the held plug's feedback and the face error, constant in K, and not a fixed fraction set by the carried region's area
gate_3_carried_depth.kind: bounds (against the closed form) and equality (its spread across K)
gate_3_carried_depth.case: porous_handover_cases.tube_reading at sqrt(K)/h 1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4; CI at D/h 16, 0.01h, half a diameter in a period of two; the probe at one diameter in a period of four, D/h 16 and 32, both interiors

prediction.value: reading / series - 1 within -4 to +1 % at D/h 16 and -2 to +1 % at 32, its spread across the three rows under 1e-3
prediction.basis: measured-before (exploration: -1.7 % at 0.001, D/h 16, 0.1h) and derived (the held plug's feedback at the line, about 4.3e-6 / 1.1e-6 of the open tube's flux at D/h 16 / 32 with 0.1h, is the same at every K below it)
prediction.why: below the line the solve does not see K, so the drop and the reading's relative error do not move with K; a carried region of area 4 h / R of the lumen's (0.5 at D/h 16, 0.25 at 32) would read that much off

gate_3_carried_depth.metric: the reading over the series closed form, and its spread over K

control.resolution: the line's 4 %: the plant is 25 times it

gate_3_carried_depth.if_wrong: an error growing as K falls would be a leak in the reading's drop (the floor) entering at a fixed size; one near 4 h / R would be the carried region's
gate_3_carried_depth.cannot_discriminate_if: the held solve flagged on every row

gate_4_gradients.claim: the reading below the line is differentiable in K and in the inflow, forward and reverse, against central differences of one discretisation, and its reverse mode passes the dot-product check through the open vessel's solve
gate_4_gradients.case: the open vessel (open_cases.open_node, D/h 8, 0.01h, steady, tolerance 1e-12), an inflow, a plug closing it at 0.3 of the line's K; outputs porous_flux and the face pressures

prediction.value: K: forward and reverse within 1e-6 of the central difference (the reading is linear in K times Brinkman's factor; the held solve holds no K); inflow: within 1e-5; the dot product <J v, w> = <v, J^T w> within 1e-10 relative
prediction.basis: derived (#264's gate 7 lines, 1e-6 in K); the inflow's line one decade looser for the solve's tolerance
prediction.why: below the line the drop does not depend on K; the inflow reaches the reading only through the face pressures, so a stop_gradient there leaves its derivative zero

gate_4_gradients.metric: forward and reverse against central differences

control.plant: a stop_gradient on the face pressures (FACE_STOP: the inflow's derivative zero) and on the permeability in the reading (K_STOP: the K derivative zero; the face pressures carry no K below the line, so FACE_STOP cannot test it)

gate_4_gradients.if_wrong: a reverse mode off the forward one is the open grid's transpose (#269's weighted product) or the face pressures' recovery
gate_4_gradients.cannot_discriminate_if: the K derivative is checked with FACE_STOP: it cannot fail, and is not used

gate_5_float32.claim: float32 gives the reading below the line within its rounding of float64 where float32's solve resolves the held plug; its range is stated where it does not
gate_5_float32.kind: equality within a line, and a measured range
gate_5_float32.case: tube_reading at sqrt(K)/h 1e-3, D/h 16, 0.01h (CI); the probe: both interiors, D/h 16 and 32, steady and IMEX Euler, iterations and flags

prediction.value: within 1e-3 at 0.01h, D/h 16; at 0.1h float32's steady solve at the line reaches its cap or stagnates (flagged), its reading still within 1e-2
prediction.basis: guess (float32's CG floor about 1e-5 against the held plug's condition)
prediction.why: the reading takes the outer flow's drop, which float32 resolves before the plug's own velocity

gate_5_float32.metric: the float32 reading over the float64 one
gate_5_float32.if_wrong: float32 is stated unmeasured below the line where it misses

gate_resolved_body.claim: a flow holding a porous plug and a resolved body (Drag.Penalty) builds, its books close, and the plug's throughflow with the body far from it is the throughflow without the body; below the line porous_flagged is raised (the forced-flow test does not see a body's displacement)
gate_resolved_body.kind: acceptance and equality within a line
gate_resolved_body.case: porous_handover_cases.beside_a_body: a periodic tube 2 mm long at a spacing of 50 um (D/h 20) in both arms, steady Stokes, one step, a bead of 150 um at rest at the first step a millimetre from a plug 0.5 mm long, K 1e-10 m^2 (above the line) and 1e-15 (below), EnergyLedger

prediction.value: porous_flux within 2 % of the run without the bead (seen before: -0.98 % and -1.2 %); books close; porous_flagged 0 above the line, 1 below with the bead and 0 without
prediction.basis: measured-before (the exploration listed), the line set after it: a fit, stated
prediction.why: with porous regions the base books the walls' penalty alone, so the resolved node must not subtract each body's own loss again (found in writing this gate)

gate_resolved_body.metric: the ledger's identity; the flux ratio

control.plant: the body's own loss subtracted from the walls' penalty again (the code before this PR): the books do not close

gate_resolved_body.if_wrong: books not closing would mean another term of the two kinds' losses overlaps
gate_resolved_body.cannot_discriminate_if: the bead's work is zero (at rest exactly): it is free, so it moves
